subsystems.name: Sample acquisition
subsystems.role: getting uncontaminated material out of vents, deep rock, brines and ice.
parts: scientific drilling rigs and borehole samplers

subsystems.name: Extreme-condition cultivation
subsystems.role: keeping organisms alive and growing while reproducing the pressure, heat, anoxia or salinity they came from.

subsystems.name: Culture-independent sequencing
subsystems.role: identifying what is there when nothing will grow in a dish.

subsystems.name: Stress and biomolecule assays
subsystems.role: measuring which molecules break and which hold up.
parts: enzyme kinetics rigs run at high temperature, salt or pressure

subsystems.name: Analogue field sites
subsystems.role: natural laboratories that stress life in ways other planets might.
parts: acid mine drainage and hypersaline lakes

subsystems.name: Planetary protection and contamination control
subsystems.role: stopping Earth life from riding along, and stopping doubt about what a detection means.

subsystems.name: Life-detection instrument development
subsystems.role: building sensors whose results will be judged against extremophile baselines.
parts: mass spectrometers for organic and chiral analysis

buildSteps.title: Pick a site that stresses life in one specific way
buildSteps.detail: A vent field, a deep mine fracture water, a saturated brine or a dry valley is chosen so that a single variable — heat, pressure, radiation, salinity — can be pushed to its limit.

buildSteps.title: Take samples without changing what you find
buildSteps.detail: Submersibles, drills and boreholes deliver material into sealed, chilled or pressure-retaining containers, with blanks and tracers to prove no contamination occurred.

buildSteps.title: Sequence before you culture
buildSteps.detail: DNA and RNA are extracted directly from the sample, so organisms that will not grow in the lab still appear in the metagenome. Thousands of genomes can be recovered this way.

buildSteps.title: Bring isolates into culture
buildSteps.detail: Guided by the sequences, researchers design media and conditions to grow the target organism, often in a high-pressure reactor or anaerobic chamber, sometimes taking months per isolate.

buildSteps.title: Map the tolerance envelope experimentally
buildSteps.detail: Cultures and their molecules are exposed to graded heat, pressure, radiation, acid, salt, desiccation and combinations, in steps, until growth or repair stops. This yields a maximum — not a preference.

buildSteps.title: Identify the molecules that do the work
buildSteps.detail: Heat-stable enzymes, unusual membrane lipids, DNA-repair machinery and antioxidant complexes are purified and characterised to explain why the limit sits where it does.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate detection against that baseline
buildSteps.detail: The known signals of stressed, sparse or dormant Earth life become the reference for instruments meant to look for life elsewhere, and for deciding what counts as a real detection.

buildSteps.title: Turn the limits into rules and targets
buildSteps.detail: Cleanliness requirements, target lists for missions and the choice of which environments are worth visiting are all set from the measured envelope.

prerequisites.why: most extremophiles have never been cultured, so sequence data is the only census available.
limits cannot be measured without recreating the pressures and temperatures of vents and trenches.
the largest habitat on Earth is rock and sediment far below the surface, reachable only by ship, submersible or drill.
in a near-sterile sample, a single stray cell invalidates the result.
anything sent to another planet must work without a laboratory, on grams of sample and limited power.

pathway.milestone: a working catalogue of environmental limits and a deep tree of life drawn mostly from sequence data
pathway.unlocks: heat-stable enzymes for diagnostics and industry, and a defensible definition of habitable conditions.

pathway.milestone: single-cell and long-read methods resolving the rare and dormant fraction of communities
pathway.unlocks: better detection of the sparse, slow life most likely to resemble what might exist elsewhere.

pathway.milestone: sample return and improved in-situ instruments on Mars and the icy moons
pathway.unlocks: tests of the limits against a second, independent biosphere — or a firm null result.

pathway.milestone: direct access to subsurface oceans through ice-penetrating probes and melt systems
pathway.unlocks: a real chance to compare an alien environment's habitability against Earth's envelope.
